rules.name: Same code on both sides
rules.statement: Two maps are scored against each other only when both describe the same code. A run over changed code refuses.
rules.risk: A change in the code would read as a change in the map's quality. A scoring run must never confuse the two.

sites.why: orders the run to stop as soon as any same-code check fails
states that a score across two different states of the code is not a verdict on the instructions
blocks the dropped-relation check when source files moved between the two maps

rules.name: Uncommitted code voids a map
rules.statement: A map built over uncommitted code can never be scored, and nobody may waive that refusal.
rules.risk: The code such a map describes exists in no commit. Scoring it badly hands the other map a free pass on every check.

sites.why: orders an outright refusal when a map's recorded commit says the code was uncommitted
says this one refusal cannot be overridden, unlike every other same-code check

rules.name: One judging setup for both maps
rules.statement: Two quality scores compare only when one judging setup produced both, so a changed setup forces a fresh judging.
rules.risk: Scores kept from an older judging setup read as a quality change that never happened.

sites.why: flags the comparison when the two sides were judged under different setups
tells the caller to judge again when the stored scores came from another setup
treats stored scores that record no setup at all as unusable
pins every doubter and every scorer to one named model

rules.name: Growth never counts against a map
rules.statement: A map that grew is never marked down for growing, because only lost content breaches an allowance.
rules.risk: A finer map would be reported as a step backwards, which teaches everyone to keep the map coarse.

sites.why: lets a count rise freely and breaches only on a fall past the allowance
scores a quality measure on its drop alone, never on its rise

rules.name: Lost check blocks, drifted number asks
rules.statement: Losing a check the accepted map passed blocks the run. A number that moved too far only asks for a human look.
rules.risk: Blocking on every wander would fail honest rebuilds, and everyone would stop reading the verdict.

sites.why: one failed check makes the whole verdict a block
a number outside its allowance makes the verdict a look rather than a block

rules.name: Code sets the right number of boxes
rules.statement: How many boxes a map should hold is worked out from the code, never from the accepted map.
rules.risk: An accepted map drawn at the wrong zoom would set the target forever, so every rebuild repeats its mistake.

sites.why: checks the fresh map's box count, and only that one, against what the code expects
works the expected box count out of the code tree at scoring time

rules.name: Missing side refuses, never passes
rules.statement: A run that cannot get one of the two sides refuses to report, instead of reporting that nothing got worse.
rules.risk: A quiet skip reads as a clean result. A run that compared nothing then looks like a run that found nothing.

sites.why: stops when the accepted map's folder is missing, rather than scoring one map alone
stops when that folder holds no stored numbers to compare against
marks the comparison drifted when only one of the two maps carries quality scores

rules.name: Frozen map, or no score
rules.statement: A map edited after it was frozen cannot be scored, so the run stops on any later change to it.
rules.risk: Anyone could nudge a map until its score improved, and the report would look exactly the same.

sites.why: stops the run when the map no longer matches the fingerprint taken at freeze time
stops when the freeze fingerprint was asked for but arrived empty, rather than skipping the check
states that editing either map during a run voids the run
